finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an arbitrary URL from the `logo` query parameter. Its only check is a substring match for "example.io", which an attacker can satisfy while pointing the request at any host. The full response body is copied back to the caller.
finding.sink: main.go:36 — http.Get(raw), default client follows redirects; response streamed to caller at main.go:38 (io.Copy(w, resp.Body))

trace.note: ListenAndServe(":8081", nil) — listens on all interfaces; no auth middleware registered
source: raw := r.FormValue("logo") — attacker-controlled full URL
validation: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") — substring, not host equality
sink: http.Get(raw) — host is whatever the attacker writes
default client follows redirects (up to 10), so an allowed host can bounce to an internal target
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) — response body returned to attacker (full-read SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: (a) Substring check at main.go:32 does not constrain host: 'example.io' can appear in query, path, userinfo, or subdomain such as example.io.attacker.tld; substring checks do not close. (b) No scheme restriction, but http.Get only dispatches http/https. (c) No redirect restriction; default CheckRedirect in effect. (d) No authentication on route. (e) No network-layer egress control in code.

verdict.guard_found: none closing. main.go:32 is a substring check (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")), which does not constrain the parsed host. No other validation exists on the path, and no CheckRedirect is set on the default client used at main.go:36.
verdict.reason: The trace is wrong at main.go:37: that line is `defer resp.Body.Close()`, and the redirect-following behavior the note attributes to it actually comes from `http.Get` at main.go:36. The underlying SSRF is real: the source at main.go:31 is attacker-controlled on an unauthenticated route (main.go:43-44), the substring check at main.go:32 is not a closing guard, and the body is returned via main.go:38. The finding should be re-filed with corrected line citations rather than dropped.
